es: Distinguir órdenes, peticiones y sugerencias en el lenguaje de un líder y reconocer cómo la forma de la frase cambia el tono.

teaching.en: Line up at the gate and wait for my signal.
teaching.es: Formen una fila en la puerta y esperen mi señal.
teaching.explanationEs: Orden: verbo base, sin suavizar. Es directa y se entiende como obligatoria.
segments: Line up at the gate
and wait for my signal.
teaching.audioText: Line up at the gate and wait for my signal.

teaching.en: Could you check the equipment before we start, please?
teaching.es: ¿Podrías revisar el material antes de empezar, por favor?
teaching.explanationEs: Petición: could you + verbo base + please. Pide un favor y deja margen para responder.
segments: Could you check the equipment
before we start, please?
teaching.audioText: Could you check the equipment before we start, please?

teaching.en: You might want to take a short break after the first game.
teaching.es: Quizá te convenga descansar un poco después del primer partido.
teaching.explanationEs: Sugerencia: might want to + verbo base. Propone sin obligar; la decisión sigue siendo de la otra persona.
segments: You might want to take a
short break after the first game.
teaching.audioText: You might want to take a short break after the first game.

teaching.en: I'd like everyone to arrive ten minutes early tomorrow.
teaching.es: Me gustaría que todos llegaran diez minutos antes mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd like + persona + to + verbo: expectativa amable pero clara, a medio camino entre petición y orden.
segments: I'd like everyone to arrive
ten minutes early tomorrow.
teaching.audioText: I'd like everyone to arrive ten minutes early tomorrow.

teaching.en: These instructions are not optional: everyone must wear a vest.
teaching.es: Estas instrucciones no son opcionales: todos deben llevar chaleco.
teaching.explanationEs: Must y not optional marcan una norma firme, sin margen de elección.
segments: These instructions are not optional:
everyone must wear a vest.
teaching.audioText: These instructions are not optional: everyone must wear a vest.

prompt.es: Hay que parar el juego ahora mismo. ¿Qué frase es una orden directa?

choices.text: Could you stop the game, please?
Stop the game and listen to me.
How about stopping the game?

feedback.es: La orden directa es un imperativo sin suavizadores; las otras dos son petición y sugerencia.

hint.es: Una orden empieza con el verbo base y no lleva could ni how about.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Podrías revisar el material, por favor?»

answer.text: Could

feedback.es: La petición cortés se abre con un modal seguido de you y se cierra con please.

hint.es: Es el modal de las peticiones corteses; después va you y el verbo base.

origin.text: ___ you check the equipment, please?

answer.text: How about starting with a short break

feedback.es: La sugerencia abre con how about y sigue con un verbo en -ing.

hint.es: How about + verbo en -ing + el resto de la idea.

title.es: Se espera que y depende de ti

es: Fijar expectativas y responsabilidades con be expected to, be responsible for, be in charge of e it's up to you.

teaching.en: You are expected to arrive at eight and sign in at the gate.

segments: You are expected to arrive at eight
and sign in at the gate.
teaching.audioText: You are expected to arrive at eight and sign in at the gate.

teaching.en: Mia is responsible for the equipment, so ask her before you take a ball.

teaching.explanationEs: Be responsible for + nombre: quien responde si algo falla.
segments: Mia is responsible for the equipment, so
ask her before you take a ball.
teaching.audioText: Mia is responsible for the equipment, so ask her before you take a ball.

teaching.en: Carlos is in charge of the water and the schedule.

teaching.explanationEs: Be in charge of + nombre: quien dirige o gestiona algo.
segments: Carlos is in charge of
the water and the schedule.
teaching.audioText: Carlos is in charge of the water and the schedule.

teaching.en: It's up to you whether you train in the morning or in the afternoon.

segments: It's up to you whether you train
in the morning or in the afternoon.
teaching.audioText: It's up to you whether you train in the morning or in the afternoon.

teaching.en: You are responsible for handing in the forms before the deadline.

teaching.explanationEs: Be responsible for + verbo en -ing: después de una preposición el verbo va en -ing.
segments: You are responsible for handing in
the forms before the deadline.
teaching.audioText: You are responsible for handing in the forms before the deadline.

Mia is in charge to the balls.
Mia is in charge of the balls.

It's up to you whether you train outside or inside

es: Reconocer elogios, críticas constructivas y críticas destructivas por su contenido y su tono en conversaciones entre líderes y equipos.

teaching.en: I liked your effort today: you explained the rules clearly to the new players.
teaching.es: Me gustó tu esfuerzo hoy: explicaste las reglas con claridad a los jugadores nuevos.
teaching.explanationEs: Elogio: nombra una acción concreta (explained the rules) y no solo dice «bien».
segments: I liked your effort today: you explained
the rules clearly to the new players.
teaching.audioText: I liked your effort today: you explained the rules clearly to the new players.

teaching.en: Next time, try to pass earlier, because that will improve the speed of the team.
teaching.es: La próxima vez, intenta pasar antes, porque eso mejorará la velocidad del equipo.
teaching.explanationEs: Crítica constructiva: next time + try to + verbo, y una razón con because.
segments: Next time, try to pass earlier, because that
will improve the speed of the team.
teaching.audioText: Next time, try to pass earlier, because that will improve the speed of the team.

teaching.en: Your attitude is terrible, and you never listen to anybody.
teaching.es: Tu actitud es terrible y nunca escuchas a nadie.
teaching.explanationEs: Crítica destructiva: ataca a la persona, generaliza con never y no ofrece ninguna salida.
segments: Your attitude is terrible, and
you never listen to anybody.
teaching.audioText: Your attitude is terrible, and you never listen to anybody.

teaching.en: I will not blame you for the goal; let's look at what we can change.
teaching.es: No te voy a culpar por el gol; veamos qué podemos cambiar.
teaching.explanationEs: Blame es buscar culpables; un líder constructivo prefiere mirar hacia el cambio.
segments: I will not blame you for the goal;
let's look at what we can change.
teaching.audioText: I will not blame you for the goal; let's look at what we can change.

teaching.en: That destructive comment hurt Leo, and it did not help the team at all.
teaching.es: Ese comentario destructivo hirió a Leo y no ayudó en nada al equipo.
teaching.explanationEs: Destructive comment: hace daño y no da información útil para mejorar.
segments: That destructive comment hurt Leo, and it
did not help the team at all.
teaching.audioText: That destructive comment hurt Leo, and it did not help the team at all.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tipo de feedback recibe Mia en este fragmento?

choices.text: It is praise: it names what she did well.
It is destructive: it blames her for a mistake.
It is constructive: it asks her to change something.

feedback.es: El comentario nombra una acción concreta bien hecha y no pide cambios: es un elogio.

hint.es: Fíjate en si nombra algo concreto que hizo bien o si pide un cambio.

origin.text: You explained the drill clearly, and the new players followed it without problems.

answer.text: Next time try to pass earlier

feedback.es: La crítica constructiva abre con next time y propone la acción con try to + verbo base.

hint.es: Empieza por next time y usa try to delante del verbo.

feedback.es: El elogio nombra lo bien hecho, la crítica constructiva propone un cambio y la destructiva ataca sin salida.

pairs: Your effort was great: you helped three new players.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige qué tipo de feedback es.

choices.text: It is praise for arriving on time.
It is destructive: it attacks the person and offers no change.
It is a useful suggestion for next week.

feedback.es: Always y nobody generalizan y atacan a la persona, y no se ofrece ningún cambio posible.

answer.text: effort | improve | blame

feedback.es: Effort se elogia, improve es el resultado de un cambio y blame es lo que evita un líder constructivo.

sentences: I liked your ___ today: you tried hard with every player.

prompt.es: Lee el comentario de la coordinadora: ¿qué tipo de feedback es?

choices.text: It only praises the writer without asking for changes.
It attacks the writer and gives no help.
It points out a clear problem and suggests a first step.

feedback.es: Reconoce lo positivo, señala un punto concreto y propone cómo empezar: es constructiva.

origin.text: The report has good ideas, but it needs a clearer order. Next time, start with the main problem.

prompt.es: Escucha al entrenador y elige qué hace con Sara.

choices.text: He praises a specific decision she made.
He criticizes her for passing late.
He asks her to change her position.

feedback.es: Nombra la decisión concreta (ver el espacio libre y pasar a tiempo) y no pide ningún cambio: es un elogio específico.

origin.audio: That goal was great, Sara. You saw the free space and passed at exactly the right moment.

feedback.es: Did not help ... at all subraya que el comentario no aporta nada útil.

prompt.es: Reescribe la crítica destructiva como crítica constructiva, concreta y con next time.

answer.text: Today you did not listen to the team before you decided. Next time, try to listen first, because that will improve our decisions.
accepted: Today you did not listen to the team before you decided. Next time, try to listen first, because that will improve our decisions.
In today's game you did not listen to our ideas. Next time, you could ask the team first, because it will help us decide better.
Today you decided without asking the team. Next time, try to ask for ideas first, so that we can improve together.

feedback.es: La versión constructiva habla de un hecho concreto, propone un cambio con next time y explica su beneficio.

origin.text: «You are a terrible captain and you never listen.» Hoy el capitán no escuchó las ideas del equipo antes de decidir.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le falta al elogio del entrenador para ser más útil?

choices.text: A warning about what he did wrong.
A specific detail about what he did well.
A longer explanation of the rules.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su actitud ayudó a todo el equipo a mantener la calma.»

origin.text: 1) Tu voz tranquila hizo que el equipo se sintiera seguro. 2) Encargaré a Tom que revise la lista antes de que abra la cola. 3) Déjame mostrarte cómo corregir el ritmo.

prompt.es: Quieres que Leo revise los carnés. ¿Qué frase con get es correcta?

choices.text: I will get Leo to check the badges.
I will get Leo check the badges.
I will have Leo to check the badges.

feedback.es: Con get la persona va seguida de to + verbo: get Leo to check.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué aspecto positivo destaca el entrenador.

choices.text: His speed with the queue was very good.
His friendly greeting made the families comfortable.
His timing with the parents was perfect.

feedback.es: Lo positivo es su saludo amable a cada familia; el ritmo con la cola es precisamente lo que queda por corregir.

origin.audio: You greeted every family with a smile, and that made them feel welcome. Now let us fix your timing with the queue.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esa pausa hizo que todos se sintieran seguros.»

answer.text: That pause made everyone feel confident

feedback.es: Make + persona + verbo base: made everyone feel, sin to.

prompt.es: Da feedback a Leo: un elogio, una mejora y un paso con have o get.

answer.text: Leo, thank you for your work at the registration table. You were calm under pressure, and that made the parents feel confident. You were also accurate with the names on the list. However, you spent too long with each family, so the queue became very long. The next step is simple: I will have Mia show you a faster system. You could also get the new volunteers to hand out the badges while you check the names. That would improve the timing, and you will be able to talk to more families. I am sure you can fix this by Saturday.
accepted: Leo, thank you for your work at the registration table. You were calm under pressure, and that made the parents feel confident. You were also accurate with the names on the list. However, you spent too long with each family, so the queue became very long. The next step is simple: I will have Mia show you a faster system. You could also get the new volunteers to hand out the badges while you check the names. That would improve the timing, and you will be able to talk to more families. I am sure you can fix this by Saturday.

Leo, well done at the registration table. You stayed calm, and that made the families feel safe. Your work with the names was very accurate. One thing to improve is the time you spend with each family, because the queue grew too long. The next step is to ask Mia for her system: I will have her show you this afternoon. Tomorrow, try to get the new volunteers to give out the badges while you check the names. That will improve your timing. I am sure you can fix it by Saturday.

Leo, I liked your work at the table. You were calm and friendly, and that made the parents feel safe. However, your timing needs work, because the queue was too long. The next step is to learn a quicker system, so I will have Mia show you hers. Next time, get the new volunteers to help you with the badges. That will let you talk to more families. Thank you, and let me know if you need help before Saturday.

feedback.es: El feedback completo une un elogio concreto, un punto de mejora y un paso con have o get, con un plazo y un tono amable.

origin.text: Leo atendió la mesa de inscripción: estuvo calmado y fue preciso con los nombres, pero tardó demasiado con cada familia y la cola creció. Escribe 80 a 120 palabras con tono amable, una sugerencia con have o get y un plazo.

prompt.es: El consejo de Ana provoca que el equipo se sienta seguro. ¿Qué frase lo dice?

choices.text: Her advice made the team to feel safe.
Her advice let the team feeling safe.
Her advice made the team feel safe.

feedback.es: Make + persona + verbo base, sin to ni -ing, expresa el efecto que provoca el consejo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Consigue que los voluntarios se registren antes.»

answer.text: to

feedback.es: Get + persona + to + verbo base: aquí to es obligatorio.

origin.text: Get the volunteers ___ sign in first.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ayuda recibirá el voluntario.

choices.text: Tom will work with him on the list.
Tom will replace him at the table.
He will help Tom with the families.

feedback.es: I will have Tom help you significa que Tom colaborará con el voluntario para manejar la lista.

origin.audio: I liked how you welcomed the families, but the queue was slow. Tomorrow I will have Tom help you with the list.

es: Coordinar una jornada de voluntariado: repartir tareas, resolver un desacuerdo con una solución justa y dar retroalimentación específica.

teaching.en: Mia, I assign you to the registration table, so you are in charge of it during the first shift.
teaching.es: Mia, te asigno la mesa de inscripción, así que tú te encargas de ella durante el primer turno.
teaching.explanationEs: Assign someone to + lugar o tarea, y be in charge of + nombre: así se reparte una tarea y se marca el turno.
segments: Mia, I assign you to the registration table, so you
are in charge of it during the first shift.
teaching.audioText: Mia, I assign you to the registration table, so you are in charge of it during the first shift.

teaching.en: Carlos, could you cover the water stall until noon, please?
teaching.es: Carlos, ¿podrías encargarte del puesto de agua hasta el mediodía, por favor?
teaching.explanationEs: Could you + verbo base + please: petición cortés; cover significa sustituir o cubrir un puesto.
segments: Carlos, could you cover the
water stall until noon, please?
teaching.audioText: Carlos, could you cover the water stall until noon, please?

teaching.en: We disagree about the schedule, so how about we swap shifts and find a compromise?
teaching.es: No estamos de acuerdo con el horario, así que ¿y si intercambiamos turnos y buscamos un término medio?
teaching.explanationEs: How about we + verbo: sugerencia para resolver un desacuerdo; swap es intercambiar.
segments: We disagree about the schedule, so how about
we swap shifts and find a compromise?
teaching.audioText: We disagree about the schedule, so how about we swap shifts and find a compromise?

teaching.en: I see your point, Tom, but it is fair that everyone takes a turn on the stage.
teaching.es: Entiendo tu punto, Tom, pero es justo que todos tengan un turno en el escenario.
teaching.explanationEs: I see your point concede; it is fair that + oración justifica la propuesta.
segments: I see your point, Tom, but it is fair
that everyone takes a turn on the stage.
teaching.audioText: I see your point, Tom, but it is fair that everyone takes a turn on the stage.

teaching.en: You handled that queue calmly, so I will have you train the new volunteers tomorrow.
teaching.es: Gestionaste esa cola con calma, así que haré que formes a los voluntarios nuevos mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: Elogio concreto (handled) y siguiente paso causativo: have + persona + verbo base.
segments: You handled that queue calmly, so I will
have you train the new volunteers tomorrow.
teaching.audioText: You handled that queue calmly, so I will have you train the new volunteers tomorrow.

prompt.es: Asignas el escenario a Mia con una estructura de responsabilidad. ¿Qué dices?

choices.text: Mia, you are in charge to the stage.
Mia, you are in charge for the stage.
Mia, you are in charge of the stage.

feedback.es: La preposición que acompaña a in charge es siempre of; to y for no funcionan.

hint.es: Recuerda la preposición fija que sigue a in charge.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Podrías cubrir el puesto de agua hasta el mediodía?»

answer.text: cover

feedback.es: Cover es cubrir o sustituir un puesto durante un tiempo.

hint.es: Es el verbo para ocupar el puesto de otra persona durante un turno.

origin.text: Could you ___ the water stall until noon?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es justo que todos tengan un turno.»

answer.text: It is fair that everyone has a turn

feedback.es: It is fair that + oración completa: el sujeto it es obligatorio en inglés.

hint.es: Empieza por it is fair y termina con la oración de that.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de la jornada con la función que cumple.

pairs: Carlos, could you cover the stall?
How about we swap shifts?
You are expected to sign in at eight.
You handled the queue calmly.

feedback.es: Las cuatro frases representan los cuatro movimientos del líder: pedir, negociar, fijar expectativas y elogiar.

pairs: Carlos, could you cover the stall?
How about we swap shifts?
You are expected to sign in at eight.
You handled the queue calmly.

prompt.es: Escucha a la coordinadora y elige qué propone.

choices.text: To split the stage time into two shifts.
To close the stage for the whole day.
To let Tom use the stage alone.

feedback.es: La propuesta How about two shifts reparte el escenario en dos turnos: es un término medio.

origin.audio: I see your point, Tom, but we cannot give everyone the stage. How about two shifts, one before noon and one after?

prompt.es: Completa tres frases de la jornada con la palabra que falta.

answer.text: in | how | have

feedback.es: In charge, how about e I will have + persona + verbo base son tres estructuras que el líder usa todo el día.

sentences: Mia, you are ___ charge of the registration table.
We disagree, so ___ about we swap shifts?
I will ___ Mia show you her system.
origin.text: 1) Mia, tú te encargas de la mesa de inscripción. 2) No estamos de acuerdo, así que ¿y si intercambiamos turnos? 3) Encargaré a Mia que te muestre su sistema.

prompt.es: Un niño corre junto al escenario. ¿Qué frase usa el tono adecuado para el riesgo?

choices.text: You might want to walk, if you like.
Stop running now and walk to the gate.
How about walking to the gate?

feedback.es: Con un riesgo inmediato el líder usa imperativo firme; sugerir o preguntar dejaría el peligro abierto.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué decide Sara.

choices.text: What time the day begins.
Who will sell the tickets.
How to organize her own table.

feedback.es: It's up to you how you organize the table le deja a Sara esa decisión; la hora (eight) y las entradas ya están fijadas.

origin.audio: Sara, you are responsible for the tickets today. It's up to you how you organize the table, but everyone is expected to be there by eight.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tu calma hizo que los visitantes se sintieran seguros.»

answer.text: Your calm made the visitors feel safe

feedback.es: Made + personas + verbo base (feel) expresa el efecto de tu calma.

prompt.es: Dirige la jornada: reparte cuatro tareas, resuelve el desacuerdo y da feedback a Sara.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's make today a success. Mia, you are in charge of the registration table. Tom, you are responsible for the water stall. Sara, could you cover the parking until noon, please? Carlos, you are expected to help on the stage. Tom and Carlos both want the stage, and I see your points. However, how about you swap shifts after noon? That is fair for both. Finally, Sara, you handled the queue calmly yesterday, and that made the visitors feel confident. Next time, try to hand out the badges faster; I will have Mia show you her system. Thank you all!
accepted: Good morning, everyone. Let's make today a success. Mia, you are in charge of the registration table. Tom, you are responsible for the water stall. Sara, could you cover the parking until noon, please? Carlos, you are expected to help on the stage. Tom and Carlos both want the stage, and I see your points. However, how about you swap shifts after noon? That is fair for both. Finally, Sara, you handled the queue calmly yesterday, and that made the visitors feel confident. Next time, try to hand out the badges faster; I will have Mia show you her system. Thank you all!

Welcome, team. Mia, you are in charge of the registration table, and Tom, you are responsible for the water stall. Sara, would you cover the parking until noon, please? Carlos, it is up to you whether you help at the stage or at the tables. I know that Tom and Carlos both want the stage. I see your point, but it is fair that everyone takes a turn, so how about we swap shifts at noon? Sara, you handled the queue calmly yesterday, and that made the families feel safe. Next time, try to give out the badges faster, and I will get Mia to show you her system.

Good morning, volunteers. Mia is in charge of the registration table, Tom is responsible for the water stall, Sara will cover the parking until noon, and Carlos is expected to work on the stage. I understand that Tom and Carlos both want the stage, so I suggest a compromise: they swap shifts after noon. That is fair. Sara, your calm with the queue yesterday made everyone feel safe. One thing to improve is the badges, so I will have Mia show you a faster way. Thank you, and let me know if you need help.

feedback.es: El mensaje reparte las tareas con estructuras de responsabilidad, resuelve el desacuerdo con una propuesta justa y cierra con feedback concreto y un paso causativo.

origin.text: Mia: mesa de inscripción. Tom: puesto de agua. Sara: aparcamiento hasta el mediodía. Carlos: escenario. Tom y Carlos quieren ambos el escenario. Ayer Sara gestionó la cola con calma, pero fue lenta con las pulseras. Escribe 90 a 130 palabras: cuatro tareas con estructuras distintas, una propuesta para el desacuerdo y un feedback con siguiente paso.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo reformula un líder esta crítica para que sea constructiva?

choices.text: Tom, today you left early; next time, please stay until the end.
Tom, you are a bad volunteer, but I hope you try.
Tom, nobody likes your work, so you must improve.

feedback.es: La versión constructiva sustituye el juicio personal por un hecho concreto y pide un cambio para la próxima vez.

origin.text: «You are useless, Tom. You never help.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Carlos se encarga de la música.»

answer.text: of

feedback.es: In charge va seguido siempre de of: in charge of the music.

origin.text: Carlos is in charge ___ the music.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué elogia la coordinadora de Tom.

choices.text: His calm work with the queue.
His fair idea about the shifts.
His help with the new volunteers.

feedback.es: De Tom elogia su propuesta justa sobre los turnos; la cola fue mérito de Mia y los nuevos irán con Sara.

origin.audio: Everyone, thank you. Mia handled the queue calmly, and Tom's idea about the shifts was fair. Tomorrow, I will have Sara show the new volunteers the tables.
